Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 100, English)
A New Third Eye Batch Begins: Dabna, the Sankalp Roll Call, and the Dimensions Teaching Revisited

This session opens the first day of a new Thir d Eye advanced batch (following the batch documented in Sessions 95–96, which had by this point completed). It r eprises much of the dimensions/mantra-physics framework taught earlier , deliver ed fr esh for this new cohort using a new illustrative example, and closes with a pr omise to continue the following day .
Part A — An Individual Note and a Warning to New Participants

1. Opening — an individual dosha note: As is customary at the start of a Third Eye batch (see also Session 95), the speaker opens by addressing one devotee's specific situation, noting they carry a Kaal Sarp Dosh that is preventing their ef forts from completing, and telling them this dosha will specifically need to be addressed.

2. A warning to devotees traveling in for this batch: Devotees who are traveling to participate are told not to treat this sadhna lightly — it is described as an unusually intense practice — and are instructed not to leave their designated seat/spot during the practice period.
3. You will be tested: The speaker states plainly that participants will be tested "in every way" throughout this batch, and that this is expected and by design.
Part B — Dabna (Dr eam-Pr essure) Explained

1. What "dabna" means: Per this teaching, "dabna" refers to the experience of being aware within a dream that one is dreaming, wanting to wake up or get out, and being unable to — a pressing, trapped sensation during sleep.

2. The "ten blankets" analogy: The speaker illustrates dabna with an analogy: piling on blanket after blanket for warmth eventually creates a felt weight that becomes suf focating — a counter -force builds that makes it feel impossible to move, mirroring how a devotee can feel crushed as their sadhna intensifies and they move between levels/dimensions of practice.

3. Why intensity incr eases for repeat participants: Devotees who are continuing from an earlier batch have had their spiritual ener gies fully reset/upgraded for this cycle, which can feel more intense ("ugra") than before — attributed to these being highcaliber ener gies associated with Lord Shiva, said to come readily to sincere Ram bhakts.
4. What to do if dabna happens: If a participant experiences dabna in a dream, the guidance is to mentally chant the Jai Siyaram mantra within the dream itself as a way through it.

5. The right mental appr oach to dabna: Rather than trying to physically push the felt weight straight upward (which the analogy suggests cannot succeed), the correct approach is to remember that the "blankets" exist to protect, not smother , and to work through the pressure calmly rather than fight it directly , remembering the experience is occurring by the guru's will.

6. On being tested extr emely , befor e it changes: The speaker advises that when facing what feels like severe unfairness or pressure during this process, a participant should let it play out to its extreme rather than resist — the "opposing" force is said to relent once it recognizes the extreme has no ef fect.
Part C — Sankalp for the New Batch

1. Group sankalp / r oll call: The speaker calls a lar ge number of new and continuing devotees by name to confirm they have taken sankalp for this new 1 1-day cycle; given the length of this roll call, it is summarized here rather than reproduced in full.

2. Returning vs. new participants checked differ ently: Devotees returning from a prior batch will have their accumulated sadhna reviewed and reported back individually; devotees new to this batch will be checked from the beginning of their practice.
3. Powers r eset every 1 1 days: Per this teaching, participants' assigned spiritual ener gies are said to be reset and reassigned at the start of each 1 1-day cycle.

4. A warning against deceiving the pr ocess: The speaker warns that any insincerity ("khot") in a participant's intent toward their guru cannot ultimately be hidden — sadhna must be treated genuinely as sadhna, not as performance, since the ener gies involved are described as unusually potent.
Part D — The Dimensions Teaching, Revisited for This Batch

1. Framing — the "second phase" of jaap: The speaker teaches the specific jaap method for this stage: chanting "Jai Siyaram" aloud while holding "Ram" in the mind, maintaining steady eye contact with the deity's image, sustained over four hours, with ener gies and visiting saints/mahatmas expected to shift throughout that time. Participants are told to note whatever changes they notice in their body and state, whether pleasant or dif ficult, without alarm.

2. A devotee's practical question about r eference material: A devotee asked whether there is a source or reference they could study independently later , beyond what's taught live. The speaker's response was that anything not fully understood live can be revisited by rejoining a future Third Eye batch, where the same teaching is repeated — framing repeated exposure itself as part of the practice.

3. Kundalini as the infinity loop (r epeated framework): As in earlier sessions, kundalini shakti is illustrated as a serpent form that, when straightened, resembles the infinity symbol — a loop that has never been broken, only shifted in plane, hence "infinity ."

4. Chakras/dimensions incr ease per level: As before, each ascending dimension carries more chakras than the last (14, then 32, then 64, and so on, continuously increasing) — described here as "floors" a practitioner ascends.

5. "Up" and "down" ar e relative — illustrated afr esh: Using a new worked example (a devotee seated at one point on the globe, with others seated at dif ferent points around it), the speaker again teaches that up/down/positive/negative displacement is purely a matter of the observer's position, not an absolute direction — cautioning against literalizing a "negative dimension" as something inherently bad.

6. Earth's motion and dimensional drift: The speaker extends the analogy using Earth's simultaneous rotation and orbital motion (roughly 29 km/s) to illustrate that a practitioner's "displacement" toward higher dimensions is not static — cumulative motion (of the earth, the solar system, and the wider universe, each themselves in motion) means no two moments are ever truly identical, even when a cycle appears to "return" to a similar point.

7. The loop that can't be br oken, and gods' dimensional levels: As in prior sessions, the framework holds that this overall loop (kundalini/infinity) can never itself be broken, only shifted in plane — while individual devotees, saints, and deities occupy dif ferent depths within it. Per this teaching, Brahma is placed around the 8th–9th dimension, Lord Shiva at the 10th (described as simultaneously present at up to ten places), and Rama Sarkar (at Saket Dham/V aikuntha) at the 14th. Hanuman ji Maharaj is placed at the 6th dimension in his awakened state — yet the speaker's own guru, also operating from the 6th dimension, is described as having "brought under control" the still-higher 14th-dimension Lord through dedicated practice, illustrating that dimensional level and practical spiritual authority are not simply the same thing.

8. Mantra's staged dimensional r each (r epeated): As taught previously: 1st dimension (forward/backward only), 2nd (+up/down), 3rd (awakened, physical ef fect), 4th (+ time, forward/backward), 5th (+ parallel universes/planes), 6th (omnipresence — acting from every point at once).

9. Same plane, comparable experience: As before, two practitioners on the same "plane" can have comparable spiritual experiences regardless of how many years each has practiced, since experience depends on plane more than raw duration.

10. Session mood check: Midway through the lecture, the speaker candidly remarked that this particular batch seemed to lack the enthusiasm he typically sees, prompting a good-natured but pointed exchange with the group about staying attentive; several devotees responded that their quietness reflected active listening and absorption rather than disengagement.
Part E — Closing

1. Not everything needs to be understood at once: The speaker reassures the group that the teaching will be repeated across the full 1 1-day cycle, and that understanding will deepen with repetition rather than needing to be grasped fully the first time.
2. A vow tied to the teaching: The speaker states that as long as a participant completes this sadhna, they will in time gain access to every kind of relevant spiritual capability associated with it.
3. Session close: The speaker wraps the session for the day , noting the remaining sankalp confirmations are received, and indicates the teaching will continue the following day .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

"Dabna" (dream-pressure/paralysis) is treated as a natural, expected part of intensifying sadhna, not a sign of danger — respond with calm mental mantra recitation rather than panic or physical resistance. Devotees participating in this batch should not leave their assigned seat/spot, and should expect to be tested in various ways throughout the cycle. Assigned spiritual ener gies are reset at the start of each new 1 1-day cycle; returning and new participants are checked dif ferently (review vs. from-scratch). Genuine sincerity in sadhna cannot ultimately be faked or hidden from these ener gies — approach the practice as real practice, not performance. The jaap method for this stage: chant "Jai Siyaram" aloud, hold "Ram" silently in the mind, maintain steady gaze on the deity's image, sustained for four hours. "Up," "down," and "negative" dimensional displacement are relative to the observer's position, not absolute or inherently negative. Mantra's dimensional reach expands with intensity: 1st (forward/backward), 2nd (+up/down), 3rd (awakened/physical ef fect), 4th (+time), 5th (+parallel universes), 6th (omnipresence). Dimensional level and practical spiritual authority are not strictly the same — a lower -dimension guru's dedicated practice can still exert real influence over higher -dimension powers.
Repetition across the full batch cycle, not first-pass comprehension, is how understanding of this material is expected to deepen.
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 100, English)
A New Third Eye Batch Begins: Dabna, the Sankalp Roll Call, and the Dimensions Teaching Revisited
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Day One session of a new Thir d Eye advanced batch.

Q1. What does "dabna" mean in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it refers to the sensation of being aware within a dream that one wants to wake up or escape it, but being unable to move or get out — a pressing, trapped feeling during sleep.

Q2. What analogy is used to explain why dabna can feel overwhelming? A: Per this teaching, it is compared to piling on blanket after blanket for warmth until the accumulated weight starts to feel suf focating — a counter -force builds that makes moving feel impossible.

Q3. What should a participant do if they experience dabna during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, mentally chant the Jai Siyaram mantra within the dream itself, and approach the pressure calmly rather than trying to force their way out, remembering it occurs by the guru's will.

Q4. Why might energies feel mor e intense for devotees r eturning fr om a prior Third Eye batch? A: Per this teaching, participants' ener gies are fully reset/upgraded at the start of each new cycle, and these are described as high-caliber ener gies associated with Lord Shiva, which can feel more intense than before.

Q5. Are devotees in this batch allowed to leave their assigned seat or location during the sadhna period? A: No — per this teaching, participants are instructed not to leave their designated spot during the practice period.

Q6. How ar e returning and brand-new batch participants checked differ ently? A: Per this teaching, returning participants have their prior accumulated sadhna reviewed and reported individually , while new participants are checked from the start of their practice.
Q7. How often ar e participants' assigned spiritual energies r eset during this batch? A: Every 1 1 days, according to this teaching.

Q8. Can insincerity toward the guru be hidden during this sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, any insincerity ("khot") cannot ultimately be hidden from these ener gies; sadhna must be approached as genuine practice, not performance.

Q9. What is the specific jaap method taught for this stage of the batch? A: Per this teaching, chant "Jai Siyaram" aloud while silently holding "Ram" in the mind, with a steady gaze on the deity's image, sustained for four hours.

Q10. Is ther e a r eference sour ce devotees can study on their own to r eview this teaching later? A: Per this teaching, the speaker's suggestion was that anything not fully understood live can be revisited by rejoining a future Third Eye batch, where the material is taught again.
Q1 1. How is kundalini shakti illustrated in this teaching? A: As a serpent form that, when straightened, resembles the infinity symbol (∞) — a loop that can never be broken, only shifted in plane.

Q12. Does the number of chakras stay the same at every "dimension" level? A: No — per this teaching, each ascending dimension carries more chakras than the last (for example, 14, then 32, then 64, continuously increasing).

Q13. Is "up" or "down" an absolute dir ection in this teaching's framework? A: No — per this teaching, up/down and positive/negative displacement are relative to the observer's position, illustrated using devotees seated at dif ferent points around the globe.

Q14. How does Earth's motion illustrate why no two dimensional "cycles" ar e ever quite identical? A: Per this teaching, because Earth is simultaneously rotating and orbiting (at roughly 29 km/s), and the wider solar system and universe are themselves in motion, an apparent return to a similar point is never a true repetition of the exact same state.

Q15. According to this teaching, at which dimensions ar e Brahma, Shiva, and Rama Sarkar (Saket Dham) placed? A: Roughly the 8th–9th (Brahma), the 10th (Shiva, described as present at up to ten places at once), and the 14th (Rama Sarkar/V aikuntha).

Q16. At which dimension is Hanuman ji Maharaj placed, and what does the speaker say about his own guru's r elationship to a higher -dimension power? A: Hanuman ji Maharaj is placed at the 6th dimension in his awakened state; the speaker describes his own guru, also operating from the 6th dimension, as having brought a still-higher (14th-dimension) power "under control" through dedicated practice — illustrating that dimension level and practical spiritual authority are not simply equivalent.

Q17. What happens to a mantra's r each as it moves fr om the 4th to the 6th dimension, per this teaching? A: At the 4th dimension it can move events forward/backward in time; at the 5th it can additionally reach into parallel universes/planes; at the 6th it becomes omnipresent, acting from every point simultaneously .

Q18. Does mor e years of practice always translate to a categorically differ ent spiritual experience? A: Not necessarily — per this teaching, two practitioners on the same "plane" can have comparable experiences regardless of years practiced.

Q19. Is a participant expected to understand everything taught in this batch the first time? A: No — per this teaching, the material is repeated across the full 1 1-day cycle, and understanding is expected to deepen through repetition rather than needing to be grasped immediately .

Q20. What is pr omised to a participant who completes this sadhna, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, they will in time gain access to every kind of relevant spiritual capability associated with this practice.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the dimensions/mantra-physics framework (Q1 1–Q18) as this specific teaching's own esoteric model, consistent with the same framework taught in earlier Third Eye batch sessions, not as independently verifiable physics. The individual dosha note that opens this session (Part A) refers to an unnamed devotee; no identifying details are given in the source and none should be added. Present the "dabna" guidance as this practice's own framework for interpreting a specific dream experience, not as general sleep-medicine advice. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 100, Hinglish)
A New Third Eye Batch Begins: Dabna, the Sankalp Roll Call, and the Dimensions Teaching Revisited

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. Most of this session is dir ect instruction and r oll call, so Part III her e is short.
Exchange 1 — Asking for Reference Material

Devotee: Bhaiya, aap jo bhi padhate ho reference bhi dete ho, aapne bola bhi hai ki aap source dete ho. Kuch aisa hai jo hum baad mein padh bhi sakte hain apne aap se ya reference kahin check kar sakte hain? Koi book ho, ya aap se kuch aur mile jo hum dekh sakein baad mein, kuch explain na hua ho achhe se agar woh samajhna ho? Bhaiya: Toh fir se aa jao Third Eye batch mein, fir sikhaenge. 1 1 baar karenge ek saath saadhna, yaad rakhna — 1 1 baar mein saala kabhi toh samajh aayega. Isi bahane tumhari saadhna ho jaayegi bhaiyon.

Why this is her e: A practical, r elatable question about how to r etain and r evisit dense teaching material — the answer (r epetition thr ough r e-attending, rather than a written r eference) r eveals something genuinely distinctive about how this batch's knowledge is meant to be transmitted.
Exchange 2 — "Wher e's the Enthusiasm?"

Bhaiya: Arre kya ho gaya, saadhna hi kar rahe hoge ya kuch aur hi kar rahe ho? Is batch mein itna enthusiasm hai hi nahi, mujhe woh nahi dikh raha, warna toh har batch mein itna hota hai — "bhaiya aaj seekhenge, aaj kuch milega." Yahan sab rotdu mile hain mujhe, is batch mein sab. Devotees: Nahi bhaiya, hum log wait karte rehte hain, aap kuch batayenge hum sunenge... chup isliye hain kyunki cheezon ko absorb kar rahe hain. Sari baaton ko sun rahe hain jo aap samjhate ho, taaki baad mein aadhi cheezein chhoot na jaaye. 1 1 din ka hi time hai, toh chahte hain ki kuch chhute na, isliye us tarah se absorb kar rahe hain. Bhaiya: Chalo theek hai, bi attentive, bi very attentive.

Why this is her e: A candid, human moment of a teacher checking in on his students' engagement and getting an honest, thoughtful response back — useful for anyone in this batch wondering whether quiet listening is itself acceptable participation.
Note on Curation

Most of this session is a repeat of the dimensions/mantra-physics lecture already taught in an earlier session (documented in full detail in Part I), plus the sankalp roll call and the individual dosha note, which are summarized in Part I rather than reproduced here since
they carry limited independent conversational value or involve a private individual matter . Only the two exchanges above stood out as having value beyond the lecture content itself.
